task.name: Clean Up Legacy Architecture and Write the Agent Integration Guide
task.prompt:
Perform a final cleanup pass after the previous tasks are complete.
Remove or clearly archive obsolete implementation artifacts from the old WebView/browser architecture if they are no longer required.
Search the repository for: WebView2, HTML runtime generation, JavaScript runtime code, JSON IPC assumptions, DOM terminology, obsolete CSS-runtime instructions, documentation claiming zUI renders through a browser, outdated examples showing rebuild-based state updates.
Do not remove useful historical/theme design information until equivalent native documentation exists.
Then create an explicit AGENTS.md or equivalent integration guide intended for Codex/Claude/Gemini-style coding agents.
The guide should state prominently: - zUI is a native Windows UI framework. - ZSL/ZML is declarative authoring, not a browser runtime. - Never introduce WebView2/Electron/Chromium to implement zUI features. - Build a screen once. - Never call Build() to refresh normal application state. - Use incremental state/property APIs. - Use collection binding for dynamic data. - Use virtualized list/table controls for large datasets. - Do not manually reproduce Holo styling inside application code. - Visual styling belongs in .ztheme files. - Applications should use semantic zUI controls rather than backend-specific WinForms/Win32 calls whenever zUI supports the feature. - C# and C++ behavior should remain semantically equivalent.
Include short canonical examples showing: 1. building a screen; 2. updating text/state; 3. responding to an event; 4. updating a list; 5. using a virtualized table; 6. selecting a theme.
Finally, update the primary README so a new developer or coding agent cannot reasonably mistake zUI for a web UI system.
task.requirements: Obsolete WebView/browser artifacts removed or clearly archived (WebView2, HTML runtime gen, JS runtime, JSON IPC assumptions, DOM terminology, CSS-runtime instructions, browser-render docs, rebuild-based state examples). Useful historical/theme design info retained until equivalent native docs exist. AGENTS.md (or equivalent) created with the prominent statements and the six canonical examples. Primary README updated so zUI cannot be mistaken for a web UI system.
task.notes: Integration guide done via ZU-88 (docs/INTEGRATION.md + the 'which zUI to pull' box in README). Legacy browser code already removed; tests/check-native.py gates it.

task.name: Add Cross-Backend Conformance and Performance Tests
task.prompt:
Build an automated conformance suite ensuring generated C# and C++ implementations represent the same zUI language.
Cover every documented ZSL/ZML node and feature.
Tests should cover at minimum: parsing, code generation, control construction, ids/binds, state, handlers, event payloads, incremental mutation, row/column layout, nested layout, resize/reflow, collection sources, list/table behavior, virtualization, theme tokens, theme switching, Holo/Material/Metro loading.
Create performance/regression tests for: repeated property mutations; high-frequency slider updates; large tables/lists; resizing; theme application; initial construction.
Tests should make it easy to catch regressions where an implementation begins rebuilding the entire UI for ordinary changes.
Where possible, instrument control creation/destruction counts so tests can prove that incremental updates preserve existing native controls.
task.requirements: Automated cross-backend conformance suite covering every documented ZSL/ZML node and feature. Coverage includes parsing, codegen, construction, ids/binds, state, handlers, event payloads, incremental mutation, layout, nested layout, resize/reflow, collection sources, list/table, virtualization, theme tokens, theme switching, Holo/Material/Metro loading. Performance/regression tests for repeated mutations, high-frequency slider updates, large tables/lists, resizing, theme application, initial construction. Control creation/destruction counts instrumented to prove incremental updates preserve native controls.

task.name: Convert Holo Into the Default Theme and Add Material + Metro Validation Themes
task.prompt:
Using the new theme architecture, implement three standalone themes:
1. Android Holo - default zUI theme 2. Material-inspired theme 3. Microsoft Metro-inspired theme
The purpose of Material and Metro is primarily to validate that the theme system is expressive enough to represent substantially different design languages without modifying application layouts or component implementations.
Holo should preserve zUI's intended Android Holo-inspired visual identity.
Applications must be able to change between the three themes without changing their ZSL/ZML screen structure.
If implementing Material or Metro reveals a visual concept the theme engine cannot express, add that capability generically to zUI rather than special-casing the individual theme.
Theme-specific behavior must live in themes/tokens whenever reasonably possible.
Provide a showcase screen that can display the exact same control tree under all three themes for comparison.
Do not make Material or Metro the default; Holo remains the default.
task.requirements: Three standalone themes implemented: Holo (default), Material-inspired, Metro-inspired. Apps switch between all three without changing ZSL/ZML screen structure. Missing visual concepts are added generically, not special-cased per theme. Theme-specific behavior lives in themes/tokens. Showcase screen renders the same control tree under all three themes. Holo remains the default.

task.name: Implement Full Native Theme Rendering Parity
task.prompt:
Wire the new theme system into both native backends.
C# WinForms and C++ Win32/common-control implementations must consume the same logical theme tokens.
Implement the necessary custom drawing/owner drawing where stock Windows controls cannot reproduce the requested theme accurately.
Do not abandon native rendering or reintroduce browser technologies.
Ensure theme changes can affect: colors, typography, spacing, borders, corner treatment, selection appearance, focus appearance, hover/pressed states, tab indicators, slider tracks/thumbs, scrollbar appearance where feasible, list/table selection, menus, component sizing, shadows/elevation where supported, animations where supported.
The C++ set_theme() implementation must become functional rather than simply dispatching a notification/invalidation.
Keep framework semantics identical between C# and C++ even if drawing implementations differ.
Add visual/demo screens that exercise all major controls under a theme.
task.requirements: Both backends consume the same logical theme tokens. Owner/custom drawing added where stock controls cannot match the theme. No browser technologies reintroduced; native rendering retained. C++ set_theme() is functional, not just a notify/invalidate. Framework semantics identical between C# and C++. Visual/demo screens exercise all major controls under a theme.
task.notes: C# done via ZU-79 (every control kind, Holo+Clean, themed ToolStrip renderer). C++ (ZU-87) does palette swap + list/tree colours + custom-draw row state; full per-control C++ theme rendering (edit borders, combo, trackbar, header hover, etc.) is what REMAINS here.

task.name: Replace Hard-Coded Themes With an Ahead-of-Time Native Theme System
task.prompt:
Redesign the current native theme implementation so Holo is a theme package rather than a theme hard-coded into runtime control implementations.
Create a native zUI theme format such as .ztheme or an equivalent declarative format.
Themes must be compile-time/build-time inputs. Do not introduce runtime HTML/CSS interpretation.
Create a theme compiler/parser that converts theme definitions into native C# and C++ theme data.
Support two levels of tokens.
Global tokens should cover concepts such as: background, surfaces, text, muted text, accent, typography, spacing, density, radius, borders, shadows/elevation, animation durations/easing, icon sizing.
Component-level tokens should support at minimum: buttons, inputs, selects, checkboxes/toggles, tabs, sliders, scrollbars, lists, tables, tree views, toolbars, sidebars, status bars, menus/context menus, dialogs, progress controls.
Include interaction-state tokens for: normal, hover, pressed, selected, focused, disabled.
Themes should be able to change geometry and visual behavior, not merely colors.
Adding a normal new theme must not require modifying application UI definitions.
Document the theme format thoroughly.
task.requirements: Native declarative theme format (e.g. .ztheme); themes are compile-time/build-time inputs, no runtime HTML/CSS interpretation. Theme compiler/parser produces native C# and C++ theme data. Global tokens and component-level tokens with interaction-state variants supported. Themes can change geometry/visual behavior, not just colors. Adding a new theme does not require modifying application UI definitions. Theme format thoroughly documented.

task.name: Implement Collection source Binding
task.prompt:
Define and implement the source= concept as a real collection/data binding feature.
A list/table/tree control should be able to receive a data source and update independently of the rest of the UI.
Required operations should include concepts equivalent to: set collection append insert remove replace/update item clear refresh specific item selection preservation where possible
Do not require Build() to update collection contents.
Do not recreate the entire application UI when a collection changes.
Define stable item identity/key semantics so zUI can update an existing row/item rather than assuming every update is a completely new collection.
Make collection binding work with the declarative source= grammar.
Implement equivalent logical semantics on C# and C++.
task.requirements: Add tests covering insertion, removal, replacement, large collections, selection preservation, and repeated incremental updates. Build() is not required to update collection contents. Collection changes do not recreate the entire UI. Stable item identity/key semantics are defined. C# and C++ have equivalent logical semantics.
task.notes: DONE both backends: C# via ZU-76, C++ via ZU-87. table/list/tree source= : set/append/insert/remove/update/refresh/clear, keyed, selection preserved by key, per-row state. See compiler/GRAMMAR.md + core/PROTOCOL.md parity table.

task.name: Build a Real Native Layout Engine for Both Backends
task.prompt:
Create a proper shared layout model for zUI instead of relying on ad hoc backend-specific positioning.
Implement the conceptual layout pipeline:
measure -> arrange -> position existing native controls
Support the current grammar's structural concepts consistently, including at minimum:
row column stack/panel/container grid where currently documented sidebar toolbar status bar tab containers nested containers padding margin/gap fixed dimensions fill/stretch alignment minimum/maximum sizes where supported
C++ must gain proper horizontal row behavior and genuine nested layout semantics rather than treating most containers as simple vertical positioning markers.
On Windows resize: perform layout again; reposition existing controls; do not destroy/recreate the control tree.
Implement WM_SIZE handling or the appropriate equivalent in the C++ host.
Ensure nested containers have sensible parent/child ownership, clipping, visibility propagation, and coordinate behavior.
C# and C++ do not need identical underlying implementations, but ZSL must produce equivalent layout meaning.
task.requirements: Add layout tests for nested rows/columns, resize behavior, fill/stretch, sidebars, and deeply nested containers. On resize the control tree is repositioned, never destroyed/recreated. C++ gains real horizontal row and nested layout semantics. ZSL produces equivalent layout meaning on C# and C++.
task.notes: DONE both backends. C# = TableLayoutPanel docking engine + ZU-78 nodes. C++ = measure/arrange Box-tree engine (ZU-89): real horizontal rows, nested WS_CLIPCHILDREN containers, fill/stretch, sidebar min, WM_SIZE reposition without recreate. layout_test.cpp. Remaining polish tracked on ZU-89 notes / ZU-70.

task.name: Normalize Native Event Semantics Across C# and C++
task.prompt:
Create a single documented zUI event contract and make both native backends conform to it.
Events should carry meaningful values instead of forcing application code to query native controls manually or receiving empty payloads.
At minimum normalize:
button → click
text input → current text
checkbox/toggle → boolean
slider → numeric value
select/combobox → selected index and/or selected value
tabs → selected tab
list/table → selected row/item identity
tree → selected item identity
scroll where supported → position
focus/change/commit events where applicable
Avoid excessive event traffic for high-frequency controls. Slider/scroll/drag-style events should be coalesced or throttled where appropriate rather than flooding application code.
C# and C++ should expose the same logical event names and payload meanings.
Update core/PROTOCOL.md or its native successor to document the contract.
Add backend-conformance tests that exercise equivalent controls on C# and C++ and verify equivalent event semantics.
task.requirements: Single documented zUI event contract; both native backends conform. Normalized payloads for button, text input, checkbox/toggle, slider, select/combobox, tabs, list/table, tree, scroll, focus/change/commit. High-frequency controls (slider/scroll/drag) coalesced or throttled. C# and C++ expose the same logical event names and payload meanings. core/PROTOCOL.md (or native successor) documents the contract. Backend-conformance tests verify equivalent event semantics across C# and C++.
task.notes: Events realized for BOTH backends via ZU-75 (C#) + ZU-87 (C++): normalized on payloads, onchange/oncommit/onactivate/ontoggle/ontab/oncontext/ondrop, option values, selection-as-keys. Documented in core/PROTOCOL.md with a parity table. REMAINING: slider/scroll high-frequency coalescing.
